title: Add OS packages (.deb, .rpm) for releases
description: This is natively supported by GoReleaser but I would like to ensure we sign builds, which requires using RStudio's GPG key.

title: Add key rotation support
description: Customers sometimes ask to be able to rotate their encryption keys. None of the products support this, but `rskey` could provide an API to make it easier to implement. Ideally rotation would happen automatically on a set schedule (say, once per 90 days or year) and would not require product downtime.

title: Add KMS support
description: Several customers have asked to store their keys in a cloud vendor KMS offering. `rskey` could be taught to do this, but it would also require product-level support in order to be useful.

title: Add fuzz testing
description: Go 1.18 introduced [built-in support for fuzz testing](https://go.dev/doc/fuzz/). Since this is an encryption library, it seems like a great candidate for fuzzing, once we move to 1.18.

title: Add tests for CLI inputs
description: Not sure what the best path is for testing CLI commands, but some testing around the CLI behavior to ensure consistency is probably worthwhile

title: Better error handling for invalid decrypt input
description:
```
Type the sensitive data to decrypt, then press Enter: hellofriendthisissomething
thatisverylong
Error: Payload is too short to be encrypted
```

This error message seems a bit less intuitive than would be ideal. Ideally something along the lines of "Invalid input" / this is not an encrypted string that we can decrypt

title: Whitespace detection and removal
description:
Some internal discussion indicates that "user accidentally copied some whitespace along with the database password" is a common source of errors with existing tooling. It may be sensible for the `rskey` CLI to detect extra whitespace automatically and remove it.

Some notes:

* Doing this quietly could in theory surprise users, so we may also need to tell them in a sensible way.
* Some secrets (rarely, I'd guess) may actually need to contain leading or trailing whitespace, so we'd need to add a flag to turn this behaviour off.
* A related issue is "user accidentally copied the database password with surrounding `"` marks included".

title: FIPS-140 Compliance
description:
There is some interest in FIPS-140 compliance, which would likely involve:

* An alternative encryption algorithm, hopefully AES-256-GCM since it's [in the standard library](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/cipher#AEAD). NaCL Secretbox is not FIPS-compliant, even though it is widely regarded as better in every way. [Well-regarded cryptographers](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=20655017) seem to think AES-256-GCM in Go is an OK alternative, though.

* Building the CLI tool with the [BoringSSL fork of Go](https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/dev.boringcrypto/README.boringcrypto.md), because Go's `crypto` package is not FIPS-140 compliant. This fork is gaining popularity in the Kubernetes to create FIPS-compliant builds of popular projects (Calico, k8s itself, [Contour](https://projectcontour.io/guides/fips/), etc.). Moreover, this approach was formally verified for [Rancher's enterprise Kubernetes distribution](https://docs.rke2.io/security/fips_support/).

* Providing FIPS-compliant binary releases. Note, however, that [GoReleaser does not easily support custom binaries](https://github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/discussions/2204), [unless run in Docker](https://github.com/apigee/apigee-remote-service-envoy/blob/master/Dockerfile_releaser). Another option would be to provide Docker images using two-stage builds and the official BoringSSL fork image, [as is done by Contour](https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/blob/main/Dockerfile).

* Investigating whether downstream users of the bundled `crypt` package can be built with the BoringSSL fork, too.

Some notes:

* There are a few possible API choices here, including a build-time decision (using build tags) and a runtime "I want FIPS" decision. The build-time decision seems more consistent with FIPS in general, even if it's more opaque to users.

* I've discovered that [Docker Swarm used a runtime FIPS flag](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/docker/swarmkit/manager/encryption) to select AES-128-CBC, but from a casual reading of that package this approach would not be FIPS-compliant by itself, since it uses Go's (non-compliant) `crypto` under the hood.

* I don't want to guess whether these changes would make us compliant. We'll have to get a more formal opinion on the matter.
